As you begin a new game, you'll be immediately prompted to enter your name. Feel free to choose whatever you like - this will be the name your hero carries throughout the journey.

The blue box below is very important, because if you miss the window of opportunity to do this, you won't get the chance again after you begin your game.

Draconian Quest Options

The Draconian Quest is a series of additional restrictions and challenges to increase the level of difficulty in-game. There are no PS4 Trophies tied to using these, so unless you really want a challenge, there is no need to turn them on. This is very easy to miss if you're not looking for it, and once you name your character and move on, you CANNOT turn them on again at any other point. While you are in the character naming screen, press △ to open the Draconian Quest menu.

  • No Fleeing From Battle: This is perhaps the easiest one (not that any of them are "easy"). Without some of the other options on, you can probably get through the game without fleeing as long as you are prepared and stay ahead of the curve in party development. The difficulty of the game normally is on the average or even easy side (for experienced players), so if you really want to turn on a Draconian Quest in your playthrough but don't want to kill yourself, this is the one. Keep in mind if you DO run into a situation where things turn sour and you might get wiped out, you're out of luck and you'll have to either take the bullet of losing half of your G and continuing on, or starting from your last Auto-Save.

Please note: The No Fleeing Draconian Quest does not exist in the Definitive Edition.

  • No Shopping: You will not be able to shop in cities or at the Roving Emporiums, but you will still be able to use the Casino. This isn't as bad as it might seem, but you'll need to focus on using the Fun-Size Forge to optimize your party's gear. There are very few times where the gear available in stores will outweigh the value of what you have available to Forge, but it means you will need to also rely on foraging Sparkling Spots on the map, treasure chests, and enemy drops to obtain what you need to Forge. Same goes for curatives. Please keep in mind that you will need to turn this off to obtain the Platinum Trophy due and to obtain certain pieces of gear (such as specific costume pieces) only available in shops.
  • No Armour: This is possibly the harshest, especially in combination with the option to increase enemy difficulty. You'll have to rely solely on buffs and the like to survive, and you'll be healing and dying quite often. With enemy difficulty increased... well, good luck to you.
  • Reduced Experience From Easy Fights: This is another easier restriction, although it will prevent you from becoming over-leveled in the course of the game and limits the amount of "grinding" you can do to level up. You can easily surpass this cap by fighting Metal enemies, however, but they do eventually have a cap as well.
  • All Enemies Are Super Strong: If you're an advanced player of the series, you can give this one a whirl if you like. A common complaint of this game is the standard difficulty, so if you want some extra challenge, I fully recommend turning this one on. There will be some notoriously sticky spots, but for the most part, you'll be fine as long as you're playing optimally.
  • Shypox: This is much harsher than it seems. During battle, there is a chance that your Hero will be "stunned" for a round, leaving them unable to act. Due to the unpredictability of it, and the fact that it can leave your party susceptible during critical moments (not to mention if you are trying to do something specific, such as use Pep Powers), you'll probably end up very frustrated. This also can trigger an amusing line when talking to NPC's.

The following Draconian Quest options have been added to the Definitive Edition of the game and are not available in the original version:

  • Super Shypox: Like Shypox, only it will affect the entire team. This adds a great deal of randomness to your battles; be prepared to lose often, especially with certain other Draconian options turned on.
  • Townsfolk Talk Tripe: Adds a chance for any NPC to say something other than their set normal lines. This does not add or change anything of substance, but the extra lines might be fun for some folks. If you already know the game well and enjoy listening to NPC banter, you can give it a shot. It's the most harmless of all the Draconian Quest options. When this triggers, the line will be followed with "You didn't believe me, did you? You must be feeling even weirder than I do!" along with the "curse" sound. I enjoyed this option for the most part - some of the lines are amusing. The lines are also from a randomized pool, so you don't need to trigger this with every single NPC to see the lines. You'll likely see them all as you progress through the game.
  • Party Wiped Out if Protagonist Perishes: Self-explanatory. If your Hero bites it, game over for you! This can make your battle strategies more interesting with other Draconian Quest options turned on, as you'll need to prioritize your Hero's livelihood while focusing on taking down the enemies efficiently (and well... everything else). This includes instant-death Spells, like Whack - so make sure you're thinking of that as well. Without any other Draconian Quest options turned on, it just adds a little bit of extra urgency, but in combination with other options, it will definitely increase the difficulty a good bit since being defeated will be far more common.

If you decide to try the game with any of the Draconian Quest options, you can turn them off at any Church where you would Save, etc. The only caveat is that you cannot turn them back ON once you turn them off. This eases the burden a bit if you find it too frustrating and you don't want to start a new game.

As I said in the introduction, this guide will not be taking into account any of these options being turned on, however I will provide optimal strategies that will suffice for both playing normally and with Super-Strong Enemies active.

Once you have chosen your name, if you are playing the Definitive Version, you'll have a few other options to confirm, such as the spoken language (English or Japanese), Brightness, and another very important option: 2D Mode or 3D Mode.

2D Mode or 3D Mode?

In the Definitive Edition, you can choose to play the entire game in 2D if you like, but be aware the standard is 3D. In the Version Differences page, the differences of playing 2D vs. 3D will be detailed, but this guide will be written to the standard 3D Mode. There are many gameplay difference between the two modes.

The game will feel completely different, as if playing one of the SNES entries of the series (most specifically DQVI, in my opinion). This can be toggled on or off at any Church or Goddess Statue. I do recommend checking it out at some point, even if you choose not to start in 2D. Whether you choose to play the entire game in 2D or for any length of time is 100% up to you.

In the original version, you will go right into the cinematic prologue, where you witness the enigmatic tragedy that leaves our Hero stranded and growing up with his foster "grandfather."


Cobblestone Tor: Base

Map Key

On the area maps, I will be including Treasure Chests, Miscellaneous Items (items in breakables, cabinets, bookshelves), and Sparkly Spots. I will only note this once, here, as I am not going to include the key on each map. It's pretty simple to remember!

Blue Star: This is a Treasure Chest.

Green Circle: This is a Sparkly Spot (you will learn about these shortly).

Orange Circle: This is a Miscellaneous Item.

Brown Circle: This is a Weather-Forecasting Cow. These are only found in specific regions of Erdrea; never dungeons. You will not find the first one until after the prologue.

Red Target: This indicates Crossbow Targets that can be found in certain regions in the original version. These can be ignored if you are playing the Definitive Edition.

Red Square: This indicates a hole you will fall through in the floor (there aren't many maps with these).

If I add anything else to specific maps, I will point it out.

Treasure Chests: Cobblestone Tor

Pot Lid

You begin in the field at Cobblestone Tor - Base, with a girl in tow. You are prompted to follow a dog named Sandy. There is nothing in particular to do here aside from learn the basics of navigation and talk to some of folks you see. If you talk to some of the people, you'll find your friend is named Gemma.

I recommend taking the time to familiarize yourself with the Main Menu by pressing △. Go ahead and take the time to equip yourself with the Cobblestone Greatsword, Trodain Hat and Trodain Togs. They are in your inventory, but unequipped. You do not need to equip the Greatsword, but it has higher Attack for the time being. It also pays to read some of the material under Traveller's Tips in the Misc portion of the menu. This is your main source of tutorial material throughout the game, so if you have any questions, you should check this out. I'll also include tips for you as we progress.

Redeemable Content and Battle Speed

Go to Misc --> System Settings --> Claim Special Rewards when you first have control of the Hero.

Depending on which Definitive Edition you are playing (thanks for making this even more difficult to document, Square-Enix), you will have an exclusive Outfit(s) that is redeemable. In the Switch version, you will have the Wolf Wear Outfit for Erik and the Baby Boar Outfit for Veronica. If you are not playing the Definitive Version on the Switch, you will only find the Baby Boar Outfit for Veronica (PS4, PC). Aside from some graphic quality (which I am not going to get into), this appears to be the only truly discrepant thing between the Definitive Editions. No word yet on whether or not they plan to include the Wolf Wear Outfit for the PS4/PC version.

The Trodain Set is redeemable in all versions (Trodain Bandana and Trodain Togs). The Happy Adventurer's Set (Seed of Skill x5 and Pep Pop x5) is PS4/PC exclusive. You should go ahead and equip the Trodain gear immediately, but hang on to the other things. In the Switch version, you will find the Champion's Pack instead of the Happy Adventurer's Set, which includes two additional items compared to the Adventurer's Set: The Eleveating Vest and Arriviste's Vest. Both are decent things to begin with, but can be obtained later in the game.

In the original version, you had access to the Supplicant and Healer Accessories as redeemable content, but this is not included in either of the Definitive Editions.

Also new to the Definitive Edition, you can adjust the Battle Speed. Under Misc --> System Settings --> Battle Mode, you can increase the battle speed from Normal to Fast or Ultra-Fast. This is a massive quality of life upgrade compared to the original version of the game. Ultra-Fast is great for farming or grinding, and paces well with using Follow Orders all of the time. It can be a fantastic default setting once you really get into your pacing, and not to mention a big time-saver. If you want to see a little more detail on the battlefield, you can choose Fast, but honestly, in my experience so far, there is no reason to not play on Ultra-Fast.

Toward the stairs, you'll find a woman with a pink speech bubble over her head - keep an eye out for these folks throughout the game, as they will have important info for you on quests, objectives, etc. She gives you a tip about the ability to change your direction while viewing the Map, which is handy if you are trying to orient what you are looking at on-screen vs. the map. Up the stairs, you'll run into Dunstan and Amber. You're instructed to travel to the top of Tor to give your thanks to the Great Land Spirit. Follow Sandy across the bridge and continue for a short scene with Gemma, and you'll be thrust automatically into your first battle!

You will be fighting three Slimes. Your trusty dog Sandy will give you some assistance in this battle, but it's going to be easy regardless. They have about 8 HP a piece, so just keep attacking and they will go down fast.

After the battle, head south to the monument on the south portion of the map. You'll find your first treasure chest containing a Pot Lid behind the monument, which is a Shield. This will bump your Defense a little, but I recommend using the Greatsword for now. The Hero can either use a One-Handed Sword and a Shield, or a Two-Handed Greatsword, but not both. If you equip the Greatsword, you cannot equip a Shield. Keep this in mind in terms of equipment as you progress.

Follow Sandy into Cobblestone Tor.


Cobblestone Tor

Enemies to Encounter: Cobblestone Tor
Slime
Needler
Sparkly Spots: Cobblestone Tor
Medicinal Herb
Copper Ore
Pink Pine

Consider this an intro to dungeons. Proceed across the log spanning the gap. To your right (north on the map), you can climb up the ledge and find a Medicinal Herb by checking out the sparkling spot you see on the ground. You'll find these spots all throughout dungeons and the field, so always keep an eye out. These spots also regenerate in about 15 minutes or so, so you can always come back and keep picking them up if you are in need of something. You can check the Traveller's Tips in the Misc. portion of the menu for more info on this. Medicinal Herbs can be used in battle or outside of battle in the Items menu to restore a small amount of HP.

When you approach the Slime ahead of you, you'll receive a quick tutorial on how to get a Preemptive Strike on enemies. Different enemies have different fields of detection, and how you approach them will vary. Go ahead and take out the Slime here and keep moving. Sandy will be helping you out in battle here, so you have a really wide margin of error in battle. He will not die in battle, which makes him a little fluffy damage sponge!
